stem: According to DSM-5-TR, by what age must symptoms of ADHD be present to meet diagnostic criteria?

options.text: By the start of secondary school

explanation: Prior to 12 years of age is the DSM-5-TR age threshold for the onset of ADHD symptoms required for diagnosis.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because DSM-5-TR requires several ADHD symptoms to have been present before 12 years of age.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because 7 years of age was the older DSM cutoff, not the current DSM-5-TR criterion.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because ADHD is not defined by symptoms being present at birth.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because symptoms must begin earlier than the start of secondary school in many children, but the diagnostic threshold is specifically before 12 years of age.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because 16 years of age is later than the DSM-5-TR onset threshold for ADHD.

source.hint: The criteria specify a deadline in the transition between late childhood and early adolescence.
